title: FPGA-LDO A V12, the Option B router V2 and the Frontend still follow pin map V5, so 6 top-chip outputs per port (12 per stack) reach no FPGA pin and ASIC3/4/7/8 cannot be fully read; their SPI, latch and clock inputs already reach FPGA balls and need only a new pin file.
what: V4 keeps the ASIC designer's pin order. The even-row pins carry the top chips' 22 outputs and their own SPI data, clock and latch inputs. The boards above still expect the older order (pin map V5). On each FPGA-LDO port: 6 top-chip outputs land on pins the FPGA-LDO board leaves open; 18 lines arrive under another signal's name; the top chips' SPI_DINL/DINR, SPI_CLK and SPI_LATCH inputs meet FPGA input lines, so nothing drives them; and the two returned 32 MHz clocks land on balls that are not clock-capable (they cannot feed the FPGA clock network directly). Pin map V6 fixes this on FPGA-LDO A and the Frontend. Option B's 120-pin J5 has no spare contact for the 12 extra lines.
where: ASIC J3/J4 even pins 2-32 and 58-72 on both V4 boards (J3.n = J4.n on 80/80). FPGA-LDO A V12 and router V2 J3/J4: pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 24 and 58 are unconnected. Pins 10-22, 26-32 and 60-72 are named for V5; for example J3.70 /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out and J3.72 /ASIC7_SYNC meet T_SPI_LATCH and T_SPI_CLK. Returned clocks on pins 12 and 62 land on balls U16 and L4 (J3 port) and B17 and R7 (J4 port). Also affected: Frontend U1 and Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc.
evidence: known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv, Option A, per port: 6 NEW ROUTE (pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 = READ, DATA8, DATA7, DATA6 and DATA2 of one top chip and DATA6 of the other); 16 renames plus 2 renames marked 'clock not on CC ball' (pins 12, 62); 4 unchanged (74-80); 13 rail and ground pins. Option B is identical. Re-read in this pass, exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv and exports/ldo_b_router/connectors.csv: J3/J4 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are 'unconnected-(J3-PadN)'; pin 70 is /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out (J4: /ASIC3_...); pin 72 is /ASIC7_SYNC. V4 dumps: the top chips drive exactly the 22 even pins 2-14, 20-32, 58-64 and 74-80. T_SPI_DINR/L(2) are on 16/18, T_SPI_DINR/L on 66/68, T_SPI_LATCH on 70 and T_SPI_CLK on 72. Spare capacity, per REVIEW_BRIEF_V2.md: 15 spare FPGA-LDO A J1/J2 contacts, 28 free Frontend I/O balls, Option B J5 120/120 used.
source: Project files: known/asic_open.json A-P; known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv and exports/ldo_b_router/connectors.csv; boards/asic_top|asic_bottom/PCB.kicad_pcb; boards/asic_top/Pins.xlsx (designer's sheet: SPI_DL/SPI_DR 'Not Shared'); inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc; REVIEW_BRIEF_V2.md. Clock-capable inputs are the SRCC/MRCC pins per AMD UG472, 7 Series FPGAs Clocking Resources (from memory, not re-read), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug472_7Series_Clocking.
consequence: Half the ASICs in every stack (ASIC3/4/7/8) cannot be set up or fully read, and their SPI inputs float. Firmware cannot repair this. It needs new copper on FPGA-LDO A and the Frontend before either board is ordered, and Option B cannot carry it as drawn.
suggested_action: Draw pin map V6 on FPGA-LDO A V13 and the Frontend in one pass: 12 new routes, the renames, and clock-capable balls for pins 12/62. Decide pins 70/72 first (AB-28) and add the latch pull-downs (AB-27). Write the V6 ASIC numbering, DATA order and per-chip SPI, plus clock constraints for the eight returned clocks, into the new pin file. Decide whether Option B continues.
verification: Re-checked in this pass against both V4 boards (which pins each board's chips drive, and the SPI nets) and against exports/ldo_a and exports/ldo_b_router connectors.csv. Per-port counts recounted from known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv.
also_known_as: A-P; pair-power F1; pair-stacking F1; pair-stacking F3; R2S-09 (firmware map); SYS-05/LDOA-03 reopened (the R2E-07 and R2S-08 closures were for the V3 pin order)

title: 20 (top) / 22 (bottom) F.Cu-to-In2..In8 blind vias (0.35-1.41 mm deep, 0.15 mm hole) are deeper than any laser or controlled-depth process JLCPCB or PCBWay lists; 16/19 sit on the B.Cu control bus, 4/3 have no copper below them, and 0.8 mm alone does not fix them.
what: V4 turned 28 (top) / 26 (bottom) of the 48 deep blind vias into through vias. The rest are rail and DGND drops that start on F.Cu and stop on In2 to In8, 0.35-1.41 mm deep in a 0.15 mm hole. Neither laser vias (drilled by laser through one thin dielectric at a time) nor controlled-depth drilling (a mechanical drill stopped at a set depth) can reach that far in this stack. Each span below In1 crosses a 0.1825 mm core, which is thicker than both fabricators' laser limits. At 0.8 mm only the four In2/In3 vias could become stacked microvias. In4-In8 would need 4-8 laser levels, beyond JLCPCB's third order; for In7/In8 that is also beyond PCBWay's 6+N+6.
evidence: vias.csv and pcbnew dumps (a review working file (not published) and bottom.json; sha256 3a97f75b…, 5aad0767…): 327 through vias and 119 F.Cu-In1 vias per board. F.Cu-In2..In8 counts are 2/2/2/2/2/2/8 (top) and 2/2/2/3/2/2/9 (bottom), all 0.15/0.25 mm, with 0 crossing span pairs. Depth and depth-to-hole ratio at 1.6 mm (Cu 0.035, prepreg 0.1, core 0.1825 mm): In2 0.353 mm, 2.4:1, up to In8 1.410 mm, 9.4:1. At 0.8 mm: 0.18 mm, 1.2:1, up to 0.68 mm, 4.5:1 (a review working file (not published), blind_vias_*.csv). JLCPCB's 3+N+3 build needs a 0.30 mm buried core plus six 0.05 mm build-up layers, about 0.83 mm thick. PCBWay lists builds up to 6+N+6, so In7/In8 (10 top / 11 bottom vias) are beyond it. The fix plan's A-0b bus re-route estimate was made on V3, with the bottom board at its crossing limit; it has to be redone on V4.
source: JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ' (last updated 9 Nov 2026), FAQ 5 and 8: laser dielectric 0.05-0.127 mm, depth:diameter ≤ 1:1, 1st-3rd order, buried core ≥ 0.30 mm, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq. JLCPCB PCB Capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay HDI PCBs (1+N+1 to 6+N+6; laser dielectric ≤ 0.15 mm), https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html. PCBWay blog 'Meet New Special PCB Technologies in PCBWay', depth control 1.3:1, https://www.pcbway.com/blog/PCB_Manufacturing_Information/Meet_New_Special_PCB_Technologies_in_PCBWay_.html. All read 11 Nov 2026. Project: known/asic_open.json A-0; known/r2-layout.json R2L-01; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json A-0b; known/pair-layout.json (0.8 mm stack).
consequence: Neither fabricator can quote the boards as drawn. JLCPCB would refuse them or split the spans into a stack it does not offer.
suggested_action: Re-route the B.Cu control bus between the dies on V4, redoing the A-0b crossing count for 20/22 vias, and make all of them through vias at either thickness. Then get the chosen fabricator's written list of accepted spans.
verification: Spans, counts and coordinates re-checked on both V4 files in this pass. The depth and 0.8 mm laser-level analysis is from the layout-fab finding, verified by an independent skeptic.

title: The top board's 28 chip lines on In4 run inside the REF_VCM plane, between the REF_VDD and VDD10/VDD_DRIVER planes. They couple about 5.4-5.8 pF into REF_VDD, 9.4-10 pF into In5 and 2.4-2.8 pF into REF_VCM, and a DGND pour on In4 alone removes only about a third of the plane coupling.
what: Only the top board routes its chips' outputs and SPI lines on an inner layer: In4, which is otherwise the REF_VCM reference plane. The layers next to it are supply planes, not ground. REF_VDD on In3 lies 0.18 mm above, over 125 of the 136 mm of line, and VDD10/VDD_DRIVER on In5 lies 0.10 mm below, under 123 mm. So most of each edge's field and return current lands on REF_VDD and VDD10/VDD_DRIVER, which reach ground only through capacitors to AGND. Five lines also cross the VDD10/VDD_DRIVER split on In5, and 24 pairs of segments on different nets run closer than three line widths. A-6's remedy, a DGND pour on In4, only diverts the sideways part.
evidence: In this pass (check_b.py on V4): In4 has 130 segments on 28 nets, 136.37 mm, all 0.0762 mm wide. Under the lines, In5 is VDD_DRIVER for 63.0 mm, VDD10 for 59.9 mm and empty for 13.5 mm. Five segments cross the split. 24 different-net parallel pairs run under 3W (0.229 mm), 22.6 mm in total; the closest is T_D<4>(2)/T_D<3>(2) at 0.108 mm. The bottom board has 0 In4 tracks. Field solve (a review working file (not published), stack from the file, er 4.5), per mm of line: 0.031-0.052 pF to In3, 0.056-0.090 pF to In5, and 0.079 pF (at 0.076 mm) down to 0 pF to the coplanar REF_VCM. Weighted totals: about 5.4-5.8 pF into REF_VDD (about 5 pF of it from the 22 readout lines), about 9.4-10.0 pF into In5, and 2.4-2.8 pF into REF_VCM. In the best case, a DGND pour 0.076 mm from both sides of every line still leaves 3.9 pF and 6.9 pF, and about a quarter of the line edges have no room for a pour strip. Eighteen lines switching together in about 1 ns push roughly 6 mA into REF_VDD.
source: Board file boards/asic_top/PCB.kicad_pcb (saved fills); a review working file (not published) and xsec_in4.py; a review working file (not published) Engineering judgement: a line's return current divides between the nearest conductors in proportion to its capacitance to each. Project: known/asic_open.json A-6; known/r2-elec.json R2E-01; known/pair-power.json F2; known/pair-layout.json F7 and F8.
consequence: Readout-synchronous, data-dependent spikes reach REF_VDD and VDD_DRIVER (and REF_VCM) of the top chips (ASIC3/4/7/8). For scale, a 12-bit LSB is about 0.37 mV and the front-end noise target is 4-5 µVrms. This shows only on built boards, and fixing it later means a top-board respin.
suggested_action: Decide with the ASIC designer before ordering the top board. Shield the y 69.9-75.0 band with ground on In3 and In5, or move the signal field next to DGND; a DGND pour on In4 alone is not enough. If the board is built as received, plan to measure REF_VDD, VDD_DRIVER and REF_VCM noise with readout running.
verification: Coupling verified by an independent skeptic (numbers corrected). In4 geometry, In5 coverage, split crossings and 3W pairs re-measured on V4 in this pass.
also_known_as: A-6; R2E-01; pair-power F2; pair-layout F7; pair-layout F8; R2S-05 (In4 part)

title: Each stack's 44 chip outputs return through only two DGND contacts at each 80-pin joint, AGND and DGND never meet on either V4 ASIC board, and the six spare pins that were meant to add grounds now carry top-chip outputs.
what: Each 80-pin joint has AGND only on pins 42/44 and DGND only on 46/48. In a stack, the return current of four chips' 44 outputs flows through those two DGND contacts at the FPGA-LDO joint, and the far board's 22 outputs cross a second joint with the same returns. A signal that changes layer between F.Cu (over AGND on In1) and B.Cu (over DGND on In8) needs its return current to jump between the two grounds. No capacitor or tie joins AGND and DGND on either board, so that return goes through the connector or the dies. R2S-05 proposed tying the spare pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 to ground, but in V4 and pin map V6 those pins carry top-chip outputs.
where: Both V4 boards: J3/J4 pins 42/44 (/AGND) and 46/48 (/DGND). FPGA-LDO A and router: 42/44 AGND, 46/48 GND; AGND meets GND at NT1 (Option A) or behind J5 (Option B). Pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are T_READ(2), T_D<8>(2), T_D<7>(2), T_D<6>(2), T_D<2>(2) and T_D<6>.
evidence: In this pass: ground-pin and spare-pin nets read from both V4 boards. No capacitor has both /AGND and /DGND pads (the rails go to AGND, DVDD to DGND). FPGA-LDO A/router pins 46/48 are GND (exports/ldo_a and exports/ldo_b_router connectors.csv). R2S-05's order-of-magnitude estimate assumes 1.5 ns edges, about 12 pF per line and 0.4 nH for two contacts. On that basis 32 data lines switching together draw about 0.38 A and bounce each joint about 0.1 V, so the far chips sit about 0.2 V off the FPGA's ground. pair-power F5: 53 (bottom) / 31 (top) connector signal nets change between F.Cu and B.Cu. The fix-plan critic notes that the DGND-on-spare items conflict with V6.
source: Engineering judgement. Project: known/r2-system.json R2S-05; known/pair-power.json F5; known/asic.json ASIC-20; known/system.json SYS-23 and SYS-41; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (critic, 'conflicts'); known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv.
consequence: Digital edge current flows through the ASICs' analog ground and reference supplies and through NT1. That can add noise to all eight recordings and disturb the returned clocks.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether AGND and DGND are joined on the die, and whether a few AGND-DGND capacitors near the connector are acceptable. Otherwise accept the pin map and plan AGND-DGND noise and ground-bounce measurements at bring-up.
verification: Ground-pin nets, spare-pin use and the absence of any AGND-DGND part re-checked on both V4 boards in this pass. Magnitudes are from R2S-05 (V3, same ground pins).
also_known_as: R2S-05; pair-power F5; ASIC-20; SYS-23; SYS-41

title: All 119 AGND F.Cu-to-In1 blind vias on each board break JLCPCB's published HDI blind-via rules: they have 0.25 mm pads on 0.15 mm holes, and some sit too close to the edge or to other holes.
what: Each board stitches the F.Cu AGND pour to In1 with 119 one-level blind vias. Each is drawn as a 0.15 mm hole in a 0.25 mm pad, which leaves a 0.05 mm copper ring. Blind vias are made by laser, and JLCPCB asks for a pad at least 0.15 mm larger than the hole, 0.30 mm here. Five of these vias also sit closer to the routed edge than JLCPCB's 0.35 mm. 18 hole pairs involving them are closer than its 0.24 mm spacing for different nets, and one same-net pair is closer than its 0.13 mm. The fix plan's step to resize them (A-0a) was not carried into V4. At PCBWay the 0.05 mm ring falls in the general high-difficulty tier already covered by AB-05.
evidence: board_stats.txt shows 'Micro vias: 0' and 139/141 blind vias. vias.csv shows span 1-2 at 0.15/0.25 mm, 119 per board, all /AGND. Against JLCPCB: the 0.1 mm dielectric is inside 0.05-0.127 mm, the 0.15 mm hole is larger than the 0.1 mm dielectric, and the 0.9:1 depth ratio is within 1:1, so these pass. The 0.25 mm pad is under 0.30 mm and fails on 119/119. 111 of the 119 have room for a 0.30 mm pad (a review working file (not published)). 18 different-net hole pairs are under 0.24 mm, the closest 0.176 mm (via_rules.py). Resizing to 0.10/0.25 mm (0.075 mm ring) needs no extra room and leaves 4 edge vias and 12 close pairs. It sits exactly at JLCPCB's 1:1 dielectric limit, which FAQ 5 allows but the table's row G does not.
source: JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ' (last updated 9 Nov 2026), FAQ 5, 8 and 9. Its rules: blind-via pad ≥ hole + 0.15 mm, dielectric 0.05-0.127 mm, hole larger than dielectric, depth:diameter ≤ 1:1, blind via to routed edge ≥ 0.35 mm, hole edges ≥ 0.24 mm apart for different nets and ≥ 0.13 mm for the same net. https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq (values re-read on the page by the merge re-check). JLCPCB PCB Capabilities (HDI 1-3 step; laser blind vias 0.075-0.15 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced item 17 (via ring < 3 mil is high difficulty), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. PCBWay Advanced PCB Capabilities (minimum ring 3 mil), https://www.pcbway.com/advanced-pcb-capabilities.html. Project: known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json item A-0a.
consequence: Even after AB-02 is fixed, JLCPCB will query or refuse the board, or enlarge the pads itself into the 0.0762 mm gaps.
suggested_action: Enlarge the pads of the 111 vias that have room to 0.30 mm. Move the 11 that lack room or sit within 0.35 mm of the edge, and the 0.119 mm pair. Alternatively, get the chosen fabricator's written yes for 0.15/0.25 mm (or 0.10/0.25 mm) laser vias. Add a .kicad_dru with the blind-via pad, 0.35 mm edge and 0.24 mm hole-spacing rules so DRC checks them.
verification: Verified by an independent skeptic, with one correction: PCBWay's 0.05 mm ring limit is the general via-ring tier, not a laser-via rule. Re-checked in this pass: 119 F.Cu-In1 AGND vias at 0.15/0.25 mm and the five hole-to-edge distances (0.188-0.335 mm) on both V4 boards (a review working file (not published)).
also_known_as: A-0a (fix plan, not applied); R2L-01 (its 0.10/0.25 mm laser suggestion); A-4 / R2L-03 (ring part); ASIC-09 (ring part)

title: On each board 40 via rings lie within 0.25 mm of the routed edge (closest 0.10 mm, hole 0.15 mm), and 19 rail vias touch their pulled-back plane only at its edge; 18 of these are the only path to the rail for one die pad each.
what: V4 pulls the inner planes back 0.25 mm from the board edge, but the fan-out vias of the outer finger columns did not move. On both boards 40 via rings lie within 0.25 mm of the edge (35 within 0.20 mm), and 42 holes lie within 0.35 mm. They carry AGND, REF_VCM, REF_VDD, VDD_FE, VDD10 and VSS10. For 19 of these rail vias the centre now sits just outside the plane's fill, so the plane touches only part of the barrel, through the kept inner ring. For 18 die pads per board that via is the pad's only copper path to its rail, and KiCad still counts the joint as connected. If the fabricator nicks the edge or pulls inner copper back a little further, these pads float.
where: Both boards: left edge x 124.57-124.63 and right edge x 145.96-146.08, y 76.2-84.2. Closest rings, 0.1016 mm: REF_VCM (124.566, 79.38), (146.078, 80.786), (146.075, 77.863); AGND (146.078, 81.14); REF_VDD (124.566, 80.37); VDD_FE (124.566, 83.51). VSS10 (124.58, 76.17) 0.116 mm; VDD10 (146.05, 76.73) 0.127 mm. Single-path pads on U01_BCD1: LREF_VCM1/2/4, LREF_VDD1/2/3, LVDD_FE2/3/4, LREF_GND2/4 and M10_L (VSS10). On U01_BCD2: RREF_VCM1/3/4, RREF_VDD3, RVDD_FE3 and RREF_GND4.
evidence: Measured on V4 in this pass (check_b.py, recheck_majors.py): 40 rings within 0.25 mm of the edge, 35 within 0.20 mm (37 through vias plus 3 F.Cu-In1), minimum 0.1016 mm. 42 holes within 0.35 mm and 35 within 0.25 mm, minimum 0.1516 mm. By net: AGND 10, REF_VCM 8, REF_VDD 8, VDD_FE 8, VDD10 2, VSS10 2, DVDD 1, CLKH 1. 19 rail vias per board have their centre outside their own plane's fill: REF_VCM 6, AGND 4, REF_VDD 4, VDD_FE 4, VSS10 1. Power-SI finding (a review working file (not published), edgejoin_out.txt): centres are 0.000-0.028 mm outside the fill, the plane meets the ring along a 0.244-0.250 mm chord, and it touches 35-46 % of the hole wall. With the planes removed, 18 of the 19 vias reach only their own die pad. A further inner pull-back of 0.05-0.08 mm (rings trimmed) or 0.10-0.13 mm (rings kept) cuts them off. A 0.40 mm inner cut-back would cut 27 single-path pads per board, including both VDD10 pads. A straight 0.15 mm inward move fits only 6 of the 19. The edge rule is min_copper_edge_clearance 0.1016 mm, so DRC flags none of this. The fix plan found that widening the outline 0.2 mm per side clears every edge via; its critic flagged the router NPTH keep-out at (112.2, 114.0).
source: JLCPCB PCB Capabilities, Outline (copper to routed edge ≥ 0.2 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ' (hole to board edge ≥ 0.35 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced row 19 (line to edge 0.25 mm normal, 0.20 medium, < 0.20 high), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. All read 11-12 Nov 2026. That some fabricators cut inner copper back 0.40 mm by default is from memory, not re-read. Project: known/r2-layout.json R2L-02; known/r2-elec.json R2E-05; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (the R2L-02/R2E-05 plan and its critic note).
consequence: Possible results: an engineering query; nicked ±10 V or reference via barrels at the edge; or, if the fabricator trims inner copper on its own, die pads on REF_VCM, REF_VDD, VDD_FE, AGND and VSS10 left floating on boards that cannot be reworked, found only at bring-up.
suggested_action: Widen the outline about 0.2 mm on the left and right (re-check the router NPTH keep-out first), or notch each plane locally around the 19 vias. Set min_copper_edge_clearance to the fabricator's value, and state on the order that inner copper at the side finger columns must not be pulled back further.
verification: Edge counts re-measured on both V4 boards in this pass; they equal the V3 values in R2L-02. The 19 edge-joined vias were re-found in this pass with an independent point-in-fill test. The single-path and pull-back figures were verified by an independent skeptic (corrected).
also_known_as: R2L-02; R2E-05; A-4 (edge part); pair-layout F2 (edge part); ASIC-09 (edge part)

title: Hole-to-plane gaps (0.126 mm) and hole pairs are below both fabricators' limits, 3 mil tracks and 0.05 mm via rings are below PCBWay's limits and JLCPCB's standard-track and blind-via-ring rules (the through-via ring equals JLCPCB's 0.15/0.25 mm minimum), and the KiCad rules equal the drawn values, so DRC cannot flag them.
what: Both boards use 0.0762 mm (3 mil) tracks and gaps, a 0.05 mm ring on every via, and about 0.126 mm from a hole wall to plane copper of another net, and several hole pairs are closer than 0.2 mm. For a standard multilayer board, JLCPCB lists 0.09 mm track/space (3 mil only in BGA fan-out), 0.2 mm inner hole-to-copper and 0.2 mm hole-to-hole. PCBWay puts these values in its high-difficulty tier. The KiCad rules equal the drawn values: the ring check is on, but at 0.05 mm; the edge rule is 0.1016 mm; hole spacing is 0.1016 mm. So DRC passes.
where: Both boards, whole area. Segments narrower than 0.09 mm: F.Cu 755 (top) / 799 (bottom), B.Cu 157 / 356, and 130 on the top board's In4. All 466 / 468 vias are 0.15/0.25 mm. PCB.kicad_pro rules: min_track_width 0.0762, min_clearance 0.0762, min_via_annular_width 0.05 (severity error), min_copper_edge_clearance 0.1016, min_hole_to_hole 0.1016 (warning), min_hole_clearance 0.1016. There is no .kicad_dru.
evidence: In this pass: pcbnew dumps and PCB.kicad_pro of both V4 boards (a review working file (not published)). R2L-03, counted on V3 with the same via size and clearance rules: 2,771 (top) / 2,816 (bottom) via-layer sites with hole edge under 0.20 mm from other-net copper, minimum 0.126 mm (0.075 hole radius + 0.05 ring + 0.0762 gap). It also found 51 / 48 different-net hole pairs under 0.24 mm. The CAF check (AB-36) re-found the 0.127 mm minimum on V4. Through-hole aspect ratio is 10.7:1 at 1.6 mm.
source: JLCPCB PCB Capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ', https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced table: inner hole-to-copper 10 mil normal and 7-8 mil high for 10+ layers; ring < 3 mil high; hole-to-hole 11 mil. https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. PCBWay Advanced PCB Capabilities, https://www.pcbway.com/advanced-pcb-capabilities.html. All read 11 Nov 2026. Project: known/asic_open.json A-4; known/r2-layout.json R2L-03.
consequence: Expect an HDI or high-difficulty quote, engineering queries that change the design, or yield loss.
suggested_action: Send the chosen fabricator one sheet (stack, 3/3 mil, 0.05 mm through-via ring, 0.126 mm hole to plane, hole pairs, fill/cap) and get a written yes. Then set the KiCad rules, or a .kicad_dru, to the fabricator's numbers so DRC enforces them.
verification: Rules, via sizes and narrow-segment counts re-read from V4 in this pass. Hole-to-plane and hole-pair counts are from R2L-03 on V3 (same via size and clearance rules).

title: Each die sits on closed solder mask over 12 capped rail vias (two each of the 1.5 V VDD_FE, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, DVDD and REF_VDD and the 0.75 V REF_VCM), each 0.077 mm from AGND copper, so no die-attach pad can be opened, and nothing tells the bonder to use a non-conductive attach.
what: With the die placed as the designer's slides show (8.1 x 7.0 mm), the mask stays closed under both dies, so each die's back rests on mask. Under that mask lie the AGND pour and 12 capped through-via pads per die (VDD_FE, VDD_ADC, REF_VDD, REF_VCM, VDD_DRIVER and DVDD, two each), each only 0.077 mm from the pour. DGND vias and 5-8 control lines also run there. The V4 question list still offers the bonding house a 'die-attach pad'. title: The 0.1016 mm bond fingers are below two published wire-bond guides and were bonded only on the one-die June board, and V4's 33 shared middle fingers (0.378 mm long) each need two opposed stitches with about 0.19 mm of finger per stitch, which nobody has shown.
what: Each die has 176 fingers 0.1016 mm wide at 0.2032 mm pitch; the side fingers are 0.254 mm long. Würth's rules ask for at least 0.150 mm width (and draw 0.300 mm length), and the EPFL bonder guideline asks for 0.300 x 0.500 mm board pads. On each side most outer-column fingers sit behind an inner-column finger of another net. Their wires must clear the inner finger's stitch from above, so two loop heights are needed. Corner and top-row end wires run about 42-65° off the finger axis. The June board, with the same per-die geometry, was bonded, so this works with the designer's bonding house. What is new on V4 is the middle: die 1's right outer row and die 2's left outer row merge into 33 shared fingers (0.378 x 0.1016 mm). Each needs one stitch from each die, from opposite sides.
where: Both V4 boards, U01_BCD1/BCD2 on F.Cu: 128 side fingers 0.254 x 0.1016 mm, 45 top fingers 0.1016 x 0.635 mm, 2 at 0.2032 x 0.254 mm and 1 at 0.2032 x 0.635 mm. The shared middle row spans x 135.119-135.497, y 76.43-83.76 (the M10/P10, DVDD, VDD_FE, VDD_DRIVER, VDD_ADC and REF_* pairs).
evidence: In this pass: finger sizes, and 33 overlapping BCD1/BCD2 finger pairs, all on the same net (a review working file (not published)). Stagger: the left outer column has 37 fingers, of which 21 overlap an inner finger in y (15 exactly in line); the right has 33, of which 22 overlap (15 in line) (a review working file (not published)). Width 0.1016 / 0.150 = 68 % of Würth's minimum. The June close-up shows one stitch per finger, and two on the double-height LDGND_11/RDGND_11. June wires: top row 1.64-1.85 mm long at up to 27°; corner singles 42-50° (a review working file (not published)).
source: Würth Elektronik CBT, 'Chip on Board / Wire Bonding - Design Rules', Version 1.2 / 12.2021 / 504618 EN, Au and Al panels, https://www.we-online.com/files/pdf1/design-rules-wire-bonding-cbt-en.pdf (fetched 12 Nov 2026, SHA-256 377d7696…). EPFL CMi 'TPT HB10 Wire-Bonder: guidelines', Dec 2017, pp. 2-3, https://www.epfl.ch/research/facilities/cmi/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/HB10_guidelines.pdf (fetched 12 Nov 2026). S01 deck slide 2 image5 (path in AB-06). That two-row fingers need two loop heights is engineering judgement.
consequence: If the bonding house cannot place two opposed stitches on a shared finger, the middle side of every die pair (33 x 2 wires per board) cannot be bonded as drawn. If it will not accept the narrow in-line fingers, none of the rings can. Either way a new footprint and board are needed.
suggested_action: Before ordering, send the U01 finger geometry, including the 33 shared fingers, and the intended wire to the bonding house (preferably the one that bonded the June board), and get written acceptance. If it refuses, split, widen or stagger the fingers in a footprint revision.
verification: Finger geometry verified by an independent skeptic (corrected). The June precedent and the shared-finger point come from the gap round (single reviewer). Sizes and the 33 same-net overlaps re-counted in this pass. The June board proves the per-die geometry, so the major rating rests on the unproven shared fingers.
also_known_as: ASIC-13 (finger size); the V4 bonding major 'finger size/stagger'; ASIC-11 (top-row angle part)

title: The opened finger rows leave bare +10 V and −10 V copper 0.08-0.10 mm apart, so an encapsulant is required, but the rows end 0.41-0.50 mm from three routed edges, which leaves no room for a dam to hold it.
what: V4 opens the mask over each finger row as one block. Inside the rows the VDD10 and VSS10 fingers are 0.102 mm apart, and a VSS10 track enters the middle opening 0.082 mm from a VDD10 finger. That is bare plated copper with about 20 V across it, on a head-worn board, so protection has to come from an encapsulant over dies, wires and rows. A dispensed dam (a bead of stiff epoxy that stops the flow and sets the height) needs about 0.65-0.8 mm of board outside the outermost bonds. Here the opened rows end 0.41-0.50 mm from the left, right and probe edges; only the J4 side has room (2.30 mm to J4's pads). So the encapsulant must be held by a fixture or by the board edges, and its height over the dies is set only by volume and flow.
where: Both V4 boards, F.Cu/F.Mask. VDD10/VSS10 fingers P10/M10 at x 124.98, 135.25, 135.37 and 145.63 (y 76.68/76.48). VSS10 track from (134.87, 76.51) to (135.21, 76.51). The left outer opening starts at x 124.805 (edge 124.339), the right ends at x 145.809 (edge 146.307), and the side openings run to y 84.065 (probe edge 84.472). The top-row opening starts at y 74.993; J4's pads end at y 72.69. The area to cover is about 21 x 9.5 mm.
evidence: In this pass, from the V4 dumps: the VSS10 track is 0.082 mm from U01_BCD1 P10_R and 0.086 mm from U01_BCD2 P10_L; M10/P10 fingers are 0.1016 mm apart; there are 11 F.Mask row rectangles. Opening to edge: 0.466 mm (left), 0.498 mm (right), 0.408 mm (probe). Top opening to J4 pads: 2.30 mm. Dam width: FP4451TD's height-to-width ratio is about 0.7, so a bead tall enough for die plus loops is about 0.65-0.8 mm wide. It must sit at least 0.2 mm past the outermost bonds (skeptic re-check). No dam ring, keep-out or encapsulation outline exists on any layer. The height limit over the dies is in AB-06.
source: Henkel LOCTITE ECCOBOND FP4451TD technical data sheet (a dam material), https://datasheets.tdx.henkel.com/LOCTITE-ECCOBOND-FP4451TD-en_GL.pdf. EPFL CMi TPT HB10 guidelines, Dec 2017, p4 (glob-top step), https://www.epfl.ch/research/facilities/cmi/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/HB10_guidelines.pdf. IPC-2221B Table 6-1 spacing for uncoated conductors: from memory, not re-read. Migration under bias in humidity: engineering judgement. Project: known/r2-elec.json R2E-06.
consequence: Without planned containment the encapsulant runs over the left, right and probe edges and toward J4, or domes above the room the next board allows. Leaving the rows bare keeps ±10 V copper 0.1 mm apart exposed on the animal, where migration can short the stimulator rails.
suggested_action: Ask the bonding and encapsulation house how it will contain and height-limit the encapsulant on this outline: a fixture dam, a mould or an edge-pinned glob-top, plus a dam on the J4 side. Make full coverage of the opened rows a written requirement. Shorten the VSS10 track at (135.07-135.21, 76.51) so its corner stays under mask. If a dam ring on the board is needed, widen the outline before ordering; that also helps AB-04.
verification: The dam finding was verified by an independent skeptic (corrected). The R2E-06 spacings were re-measured on both V4 boards in this pass.

title: None of the 30 capacitors on either board has a capacitance value, voltage rating or part number, including four 0201 parts on the ±10 V rails.
what: Every capacitor is the bare symbol 'C_Small_US' with an 0201 footprint and empty value, rating and part-number fields. So the BOM cannot be bought, and nothing ensures that C18/C19 (VDD10) and C25/C26 (VSS10) are rated above 10 V. Common 0201 parts are rated 6.3-10 V, and 16-25 V 0201 parts lose much of their capacitance at 10 V bias. The under-die capacitors sit on B.Cu, far from AGND on In1, so each mounts with about 1.5 nH; values should be chosen with that in mind.
evidence: In this pass, exports/asic_top|asic_bottom/parts.csv: all 30 have value 'C_Small_US', footprint C_0201_0603Metric, and empty Datasheet and MPN fields. Capacitor nets: VDD10, VSS10 and VDD_CGEN 2 each; the 1.5 V rails 4 each to AGND; DVDD 4 to DGND. The fix plan proposes one part, CL03A104KA3NNNC (100 nF, 25 V, X5R, 0201), for all 30 positions; this was not re-checked against a datasheet. pair-power F10 estimates about 1.6 nH for the two-via loop of each B.Cu capacitor.
source: Project: known/asic_open.json A-3; known/pair-power.json F3 and F10; known/asic.json ASIC-06; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (A-3 plan). Voltage derating: engineering judgement.
consequence: There is no buildable BOM. A 10 V part on a 10 V rail runs at its full rating and loses much of its capacitance.
suggested_action: Get values from the ASIC designer. Fill in value, rating (at least 16 V, preferably 25 V for C18/C19/C25/C26) and MPN for all 30, and check the chosen part's maximum height against AB-06.
verification: Capacitor fields and nets re-read from both V4 exports in this pass.
also_known_as: A-3; pair-power F3; pair-power F10 (mounting inductance); ASIC-06

source: Hirose drawing EDC3-311352-00, DF40C-*DS-0.4V(51), sheet 1/2, revision mark 5, engagement figure, https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=2d&lang=en&num=DF40C-80DS-0.4V%2851%29. hirose.com returned 403 on 12 Nov, so it was read from the copy saved 11 Nov: a review working file (not published), SHA-256 f8fe6b2f…. Get the die thickness and the probe-base thickness (including adhesive) and confirm that die + attach + base stays at or below about 0.96 mm under the 24 capacitors. title: Both boards still fit the generic J1 side pin at the same spot, so in each pair one tail lands on the other board's lead. That can hold the DF40 joint open by up to about 0.49 mm, using up its 0.45 mm contact travel at the worst tolerance corner.
what: J1 is a one-pin AGND right-angle header with a through-hole tail. It is fitted on both boards at the same XY and has no part number. In a stacked pair the upper board's tail comes down on the lower board's bent lead and holds the DF40 pair apart at that end. With KiCad's generic model the gap is about 0.18 mm at nominal sizes, and 0 to about 0.49 mm across Hirose's 1.5 ± 0.15 mm mated height and a ±10 % board thickness. The DF40's effective contact length (the travel over which the contacts still touch) is 0.45 mm. At the worst corner the contacts nearest J1 (pin 2 T_READ(2), then pin 1 VDD_CGEN) are therefore at or just past the end of that travel. With 0.8 mm boards the overlap would be about 0.99 mm, so J1 could not be fitted on both boards at all.
where: Both V4 boards: J1 Connector_PinHeader_1.00mm:PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal at (144.875, 68.28), F.Cu, 0.5 mm drill, /AGND. It is not DNP and is in the BOM and placement files. Its courtyard overlaps J4's, which is the only DRC error. There is one such joint per port in both options.
evidence: Re-read in this pass on both boards: J1 dnp False, no_bom False, no_pos False; DRC courtyards_overlap between J4 (135.54, 71.005) and J1 (144.875, 68.28). A skeptic re-measured the KiCad STEP model: the tail tip is 2.50 mm below the board top, not 2.55. Overlap = 0.785 − (t + H − 2.50), where t is board thickness and H the mated height. That gives 0.185 mm at t 1.6 / H 1.5, 0.495 mm at t 1.44 / H 1.35, and none at t 1.76 / H 1.65. Contact left at the worst corner is −0.045 to 0.000 mm, or 0.115 mm with a 1.6 mm board and a short connector. On a 0.8 mm board at H 1.5 the overlap is 0.985 mm (a review working file (not published)). The pin-1 end lifts first. The near board's J1 body clears the FPGA-LDO/router underside by H − 1.27 = 0.08-0.38 mm.
source: Hirose drawing EDC3-311352-00 sheet 1/2 (mated height 1.5 ± 0.15 mm; effective contact length 0.45 mm), https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=2d&lang=en&num=DF40C-80DS-0.4V%2851%29, read from the saved copy (SHA-256 f8fe6b2f…). JLCPCB PCB Capabilities (thickness tolerance ±10 % at ≥ 1.0 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities, read 12 Nov 2026. KiCad 10.0.6 generic model /Applications/KiCad/KiCad.app/Contents/SharedSupport/3dmodels/Connector_PinHeader_1.00mm.3dshapes/PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal.step, which is not the real part. Project: known/r2-system.json R2S-06; known/pair-layout.json F10.
consequence: The far board's contacts near pin 1, including VDD_CGEN and a top-chip output, can be open or intermittent after assembly or with head movement. That silently loses two ASICs per port.
suggested_action: Mark J1 DNP on the far (top) board. Give J1 a real part number whose tail ends no more than about 0.3 mm below a 1.6 mm board, and re-run the stack with the real drawing. Clear the J4/J1 courtyard overlap.
verification: Verified by an independent skeptic (tail length corrected to 2.50 mm). J1 flags, position and the courtyard error re-read from V4 in this pass.

title: Both V4 files are a 1.6 mm ten-layer stack, while the fit models and records use 0.8 mm. The choice changes stack height, probe-row spacing and the via build.
what: The files define a 1.6 mm board with 0.1825 mm cores and 0.1 mm prepregs. With four 1.6 mm ASIC boards each head stack is about 17.0 mm tall instead of 13.8 mm. The four probe rows are then 3.1/6.2/3.1 mm apart instead of 2.3/5.4/2.3 mm, and each stack gains about 2.3-2.9 g. A 0.8 mm ten-layer board is in PCBWay's high-difficulty class and leaves about 0.05 mm per dielectric. It does not fix the deep vias (AB-02), and it would make J1 impossible on both boards of a pair (AB-07). The fit and print models recorded on 11 Nov use 0.8 mm.
where: Both boards: PCB.kicad_pcb line 6 (thickness 1.6) and the stack-up block. Records: inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md (print models) and inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md lines 108-110.
evidence: In this pass, pcbnew reports a board thickness of 1.6 mm in both V4 files. R2S-03 stack calculation, Option A board top faces: −4.60, −1.50, 4.68 and 7.78 mm at 1.6 mm, against −3.80, −1.50, 3.88 and 6.18 mm at 0.8 mm. Envelope 13.82 mm at 0.8 mm grows to 16.95 mm at 1.6 mm. At 0.8 mm, ten 0.035 mm copper layers leave about 0.45 mm for nine dielectrics.
source: PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced item 27 (10 layers < 1.20 mm is high difficulty), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. JLCPCB 'HDI PCB Capabilities & FAQ' (buried core ≥ 0.30 mm; HDI thickness 0.5-2.4 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq. Project: known/asic_open.json A-2; known/r2-system.json R2S-03; known/pair-layout.json F5.

suggested_action: Decide between 1.6 mm and a fabricator-quoted thin ten-layer stack before ordering. Write the choice into both files, and rebuild the fit and print models and the head view with it.
verification: Thickness re-read from both V4 files in this pass. Stack arithmetic from R2S-03 (V3, same thickness).
also_known_as: A-2; R2S-03; pair-layout F5; ASIC-08; SYS-29

title: With the die placed as on the June board, each probe crosses a 0.47 mm strip of board with no keep-out, over all eight inner planes and, on the die face, an F.Cu CLKH track and capped VDD_DRIVER/REF_VDD vias (chip 1) or the AGND pour and five AGND blind vias (chip 2, whose CLKH is on B.Cu); V4's finger ring sits 0.31 mm farther from the probe edge than June's.

title: The V4 boards carry no board name and the DF40 has no key, so two boards of one kind tie 22-24 chip outputs together and a near board turned 180° on its FPGA-LDO port puts ±10 V on chip outputs.
what: The top and bottom boards have the same outline, the same connector positions, no key and no board name, but they are not interchangeable. A 180° turn maps pin n to pin 81−n. That puts VDD10 (+10 V, pin 36) on pin 45, a bottom chip's CLK32MHZ output, and VSS10 (−10 V, pin 54) on pin 27, a data output. Two bottom boards tie 24 outputs together (22 odd-row lines and DISC_OUT on pins 3/5). Two top boards tie the 22 even-row outputs together. The DF40 itself is not polarized.
where: Both V4 boards: outline 124.34-146.31 x 67.44-84.47 mm. J3 at (135.54, 71.01) and J4 at (135.54, 71.005), both rotated 180°. The only board text is the F.Cu dimension '21.7424', and the title blocks are empty.
evidence: In this pass (check_b.py on V4): the top chips drive even pins 2-14, 20-32, 58-64 and 74-80 (22 pins). The bottom chips drive odd pins 3, 5, 9-21, 27-47 and 73-79 (24 pins). Pin 45 is /CLK32MHZ (U01_BCD1), pin 27 is /D<4>(2) (U01_BCD2 DATAL<1>), pin 36 is /VDD10 and pin 54 is /VSS10. J3.n = J4.n on 80/80. There are no text items besides the dimension.
source: Hirose DF40 series: not polarized, as cited in SYS-09 (not re-read), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Engineering judgement. Project: known/r2-system.json R2S-04; known/r2-elec.json R2E-03; known/pair-stacking.json F4.
consequence: A mis-stacked pair can damage bonded ASICs at first power-up, and the symptom (two chips silent or garbled) does not show which mistake was made.
suggested_action: Choose one marking scheme and put it, with V4, on both faces of each board where it stays visible after mating. Use NEAR/FAR rather than TOP/BOTTOM, because the underside port reverses the picture (AB-25). Decide on a mechanical key or a written fit procedure.
verification: Re-checked on both V4 boards in this pass: which pins each board drives, the nets on pins 27/36/45/54, and the text items.

title: Nothing in the V4 package tells the bonding house where, which way or how to bond the dies: there is no die outline, centre, orientation mark or V4 bond diagram, and no wire, attach or encapsulation specification.
what: V4 correctly marks U01_BCD1/BCD2 not placed and leaves them out of the BOM and position files, but nothing replaces that data for the bonding house. Each U01 footprint has only its 176 fingers and 5-6 mask openings, and neither board nor schematic carries a note or title block. The only bond map is the designer's photo of the bonded June board (slide 2). It matches 170 of the 176 V4 fingers wire for wire, but it names no pads. It also does not show what is new on V4: two dies sharing 33 middle fingers, and seven changed fingers per die (CGEN_BK removed, DISC_OUT and RRST_DIGITAL moved to the inner row, four small moves). The die centre is not the footprint origin. The June die sat about 0.24-0.25 mm left of and 0.25-0.27 mm below it, and a die placed on the origin would reach 0.01 mm into the right inner fingers.
where: Both V4 boards: U01_BCD1 at (130.369, 80.205) and U01_BCD2 at (140.755, 80.205), footprint chip:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP, DNP, no BOM, no position file. Their only graphics are F.Mask shapes (6 and 5). Estimated die centres are near (130.12-130.13, 80.45-80.48) and (140.51-140.52, 80.45-80.48).
evidence: In this pass, from the V4 dumps: U01 dnp, no_bom and no_pos are all True; the only graphics are 6/5 F.Mask shapes, with no F.Fab, silkscreen or courtyard; title blocks are empty. Photo analysis (a review working file (not published)): 179 gold balls = 177 June fingers plus second stitches on LDGND_11/RDGND_11. The die pad ring and the June finger ring match in number, order and corner layout. 170/176 V4 fingers lie within 0.002 mm of their June positions relative to the ring. On the June frame the die spans x 126.21-134.43, y 77.12-84.16 (image5) or x 126.28-134.35, y 77.15-84.07 (image4). Placed on the V4 origin, its right edge would be at x 134.419, past the inner finger edge at 134.408. CGEN_BK, DISC_OUT and RRST_DIGITAL all carried wires in June. At their June positions on V4 they would overlap die 2's VCM, AGND2 and CLKH fingers, which is why they moved. The V4 question list asks the bonding house only about finish, die-attach pad, back-side parts and mask openings.
source: S01 'Chip_FPGA Interface.pptx' slides 1-2 (image2-image5), site/FPGA_4K_headcad/sources/slides/Chip_FPGA_Interface.pptx (sha256 7f2d6f16…0420, the same as S01 in W2/inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.json line 12). W2/inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/power_primary_evidence.json line 342 ('Bonding Map'). June Gerbers W2/inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/. ASIC_FE_2026-11-11/deliver10/report/index.html. Würth Elektronik CBT, 'Chip on Board / Wire Bonding Design Rules', Version 1.2 / 12.2021, https://www.we-online.com/files/pdf1/design-rules-wire-bonding-cbt-en.pdf. EPFL CMi, TPT HB10 guidelines, Dec 2017, https://www.epfl.ch/research/facilities/cmi/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/HB10_guidelines.pdf.

suggested_action: Add the die outline (8.1 x 7.0 mm, centred on the finger opening), its centre coordinates and an orientation mark to the U01 footprint's fab layer. Issue one bonding drawing per board type covering: die placement and orientation; a V4 bond diagram with pad names (170 fingers from slide 2, the 33 shared fingers with each die's half marked, and the corner changes); wire type and diameter; loop and encapsulant height (AB-06); attach material (AB-10); and build order (AB-32). Have the designer confirm that CGEN_BK may stay unbonded.

U01 flags and graphics re-read from V4 in this pass. Severity kept major: the photo removes most doubt about pad order, but not the V4-only details.
also_known_as: A-5 (bonding part); ASIC-03 (wire-bond diagram); ASIC-19 (changed fingers); ASIC-11 (die position part); ASIC-22 (attach spec)

title: No chip's DISC_OUT reaches the FPGA, and the top chips' DISC_OUT pads have no copper at all, while the ASIC designer has not said whether DISC_OUT must be read, grounded or left open.
what: V4 cut the top chips' DISC_OUT from pins 3/5, which fixed the two-driver contention, but it left those pads with no track, via or test point. The bottom chips still drive pins 3/5, which are unconnected on FPGA-LDO A and the router and have no Frontend line. The designer's sheet lists DISC_OUT as an output and notes that it might be grounded or used for testing. The V4 question list now asks the right question (read, ground or leave open, on all chips), but no answer is recorded.
where: Top board: U01_BCD1/BCD2 DISC_OUT (/T_DISC_OUT, /T_DISC_OUT(2)). Bottom board: /DISC_OUT (pin 5) and /DISC_OUT(2) (pin 3). FPGA-LDO A and router: J3/J4 pins 3/5 unconnected.
evidence: In this pass: on the top board, /T_DISC_OUT and /T_DISC_OUT(2) each have 1 pad, 0 tracks and 0 vias (ERC shows isolated_pin_label twice). On the bottom board, /DISC_OUT and /DISC_OUT(2) have 3 pads each. exports/ldo_a and exports/ldo_b_router connectors.csv: J3/J4 pins 3/5 'unconnected'. boards/asic_top/Pins.xlsx cells E3/E4 (DISC_OUT and the designer's note).
source: The ASIC designer's sheet, boards/asic_top/Pins.xlsx and inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 2. ASIC_FE_2026-11-11/deliver10/report/index.html (question list). Project: known/r2-elec.json R2E-04; known/r2-system.json R2S-07.
consequence: If DISC_OUT turns out to be a needed status or safety output, or must be grounded, none of the eight chips complies without new boards.
suggested_action: Get the designer's answer before the Frontend and FPGA-LDO A are ordered. Meanwhile consider adding a DNP 0201 pad from each top-chip DISC_OUT finger to ground, which keeps both options open. Pins 4 and 6, once the spare suggestion, now carry outputs.
verification: Re-checked on both V4 boards and the FPGA-LDO exports in this pass.

title: Pin map V6 adds two FPGA outputs per port for the top chips' SPI clock and latch, although the ASIC designer's sheet marks SPI_CLK and SPI_LATCH as shared.
what: In V4 every chip has its own SPI data pair, as the designer's 'Not Shared' column requires. The two top chips take their SPI clock and latch on pins 72/70, separate from the bottom chips' 63/61. The V6 plan turns pins 70/72 into two more FPGA outputs per port. The designer's sheet lists SPI_CLK and SPI_LATCH under 'Shared'. Tying pin 70 to the existing latch net and pin 72 to the port's SPI clock on the FPGA-LDO board would still configure every chip separately, with no change to the ASIC boards. It would also free 2 lines per port for unrouted top-chip outputs.
where: ASIC V4 J3/J4: pins 61/63 (SPI_LATCH/SPI_CLK, bottom chips) and 70/72 (T_SPI_LATCH/T_SPI_CLK, top chips). FPGA-LDO A V12: J3/J4.61 /SPI_LATCH_SHARED (R18; J2.48 to ball D11); J3.63 /BOARD3_SPI_CLK (J2.13 to V8); J4.63 /BOARD1_SPI_CLK (J2.52 to D10). Pins 70/72 currently go to J2.26/J2.24 (balls N3/N4) on the J3 port and J2.35/J2.37 (P4/P3) on the J4 port. Router V2 uses J5.90/J5.92 and J5.89/J5.91.
evidence: boards/asic_top/Pins.xlsx Sheet1, read in this pass: A1 'Shared', B8 'SPI_CLK', B9 'SPI_LATCH'; C1 'Not Shared', C3 'SPI_DL', C4 'SPI_DR'. In V4, /SPI_LATCH and /SPI_CLK reach the 2 bottom chips and /T_SPI_LATCH and /T_SPI_CLK the 2 top chips; the 8 DINL/DINR nets are separate. With the tie, each port needs 26 even-row lines to reach the FPGA (22 top-chip outputs plus 4 SPI data inputs) against 22 existing routes. That is 4 new routes per port (8 in all) instead of 12. Spare FPGA-LDO A J1/J2 contacts would be 15 − 12 (V6) − 2 (SYS-10) = 1 without the tie, and 5 with it. Option B would need 8 more J5 contacts instead of 12, but J5 is 120/120, so Option B stays blocked.
source: The ASIC designer's pin sheet, boards/asic_top/Pins.xlsx. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv. known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (critic, 'conflicts').
consequence: Without the tie, V6 spends 2 joint contacts and 2 FPGA pins per port on signals the chips could share. It leaves 1 spare FPGA-LDO A J1/J2 contact, needs 12 new escape routes beside U1 on the dense Frontend, and creates the floating latch of AB-27.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether the top chips may share SPI_CLK and SPI_LATCH with the bottom chips, with the data lines staying separate. If yes, tie pin 70 to /SPI_LATCH_SHARED and pin 72 to the port's BOARDx_SPI_CLK on FPGA-LDO A V13 (and on the router), and reuse the freed lines for top-chip outputs.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. The Pins.xlsx cells and the V4 SPI nets re-read in this pass.

title: U01_BCD1's VDD_CGEN pad is still 15.5 mm from its nearest capacitor, with no VDD_CGEN plane.
what: The 1.5 V rail capacitors now sit under the dies, but VDD_CGEN was not included. Its only capacitors, C6 and C50, stay east of J4: about 5.9-6.4 mm from U01_BCD2 and 15.5-15.7 mm from U01_BCD1. The rail reaches U01_BCD1 through about 15 mm of thin track.

title: The In5/In6 split puts the −10 V plane face to face with DVDD over 136 mm², and the +10 V plane face to face with REF_VCM over 99-120 mm², across 0.1 mm with no ground between.
what: Two planes facing each other across thin insulation form a capacitor that couples noise between them. On both V4 boards VSS10 on In6 faces DVDD on In7 across 0.1 mm, over about 2.3 times the area of the original PCB-5. VDD10 on In5 faces REF_VCM on In4. Stimulator switching on ±10 V therefore couples into the digital supply and into the REF_VCM reference.
where: Both boards, In4/In5/In6/In7.
evidence: In this pass (planes2.py: pcbnew intersection of the saved fills, C = ε0·4.5·A/d): VSS10 (In6) x DVDD (In7) 136 mm², 54 pF, on both boards. REF_VCM (In4) x VDD10 (In5) 99 mm², 39 pF (top) and 120 mm², 48 pF (bottom). VDD10 x VSS10 across 0.1825 mm: 81-82 mm², 18 pF. Original PCB-5 (pair-layout F11): 59.6 mm² / 23.7 pF, 101 mm² / 40 pF and 58 mm² / 12.6 pF.
source: Engineering judgement. Project: known/pair-layout.json F11; known/asic.json ASIC-24.
consequence: Likely small, but it goes the wrong way for a recording front end.
suggested_action: When the stack is next changed, put a ground plane between the ±10 V layers and DVDD/REF_VCM. Meanwhile, measure REF_VCM noise during stimulation.
verification: Areas recomputed on both V4 boards in this pass.

title: The V4 list marks via-in-pad filling as fixed, but the C6 and C50 pads keep open vias, about 170 vias inside the finger rings stay open, and the standard drill and Gerber files carry no fill or cap marking.
what: V4 marks 100 (top) / 83 (bottom) through vias filled and capped: every via in a J3/J4 pad, 37 under the dies and one in C59's pad. Two vias inside 0201 pads stay open. One is a VDD_CGEN through via in C50 pad 1, with the paste opening printed over part of its hole. The other is an AGND F.Cu-In1 via in the middle of C6 pad 2. Inside the finger rings 83-87 vias per die also stay open. KiCad writes fill and cap marks only into an optional Gerber-format drill export. The normal Excellon drill files (one tool for all 327 through holes), the copper Gerbers and the job file say nothing about them.
where: Both boards: C50 pad 1 (VDD_CGEN) holds the through via at (145.059, 71.691), open. C6 pad 2 (AGND) holds the F.Cu-In1 via at (145.85, 70.92), open. Open vias inside the finger rings: 83/87 (top) and 84/87 (bottom), for BCD1/BCD2.
evidence: In this pass: 100 / 83 vias filled and capped, and the C6/C50 in-pad vias open on both boards (a review working file (not published)). Layout-fab: C50's pin-1 paste pad spans x 145.046-145.364, over part of the hole at x 144.984-145.134. kicad-cli 10.0.6 Excellon output: PCB.drl uses tool T1 (0.150 mm) for all 327 through holes, with no fill attribute. 'export drill --format gerber' adds PCB-filling-front-back.gbr and PCB-capping-front-back.gbr with 100 / 83 flashes. Their line 5 reads '%TF,FileFunction,Other,Filling*%', with a comma where every other KiCad file has '%TF.FileFunction' (a review working file (not published)). known/asic_open.json lists P-M5 as fixed.
source: JLCPCB PCB Capabilities ('Epoxy Filled & Capped' for 0.15-0.55 mm vias, default on 6+ layers), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay HDI PCBs (resin-filled vias 0.254-6.5 mm), https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced item 23 (plug hole 0.20-0.40 mm), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. All read 11 Nov 2026. Gerber X2 attribute syntax: from memory, not re-read. Project: known/r2-layout.json R2L-05.

suggested_action: Mark the C6 and C50 vias filled and capped, plus every via inside the finger rings if the bonding house wants it. State the requirement on the order ('IPC-4761 Type VII, all vias', or the list with a drawing) rather than relying on the KiCad flags or the optional filling Gerbers.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. Fill counts and the C6/C50 vias re-checked on both V4 boards in this pass.
also_known_as: R2L-05; contradicts P-M5; ASIC-10 (0201 part); ASIC-22 (open vias under the dies); pair-layout F3 (C6/C50 part)

title: The finger-row mask openings end 0-0.05 mm from 61-63 open fan-out via rings per board, and five rings already reach into an opening.
what: V4 keeps V3's row openings with a 0.05 mm margin. The fan-out vias sit only 0.076-0.14 mm beyond the finger ends, so the mask left over them is 0-0.05 mm wide, and normal mask misregistration will expose more rings. About half of the near vias carry a different net from the nearest finger, and all of them are open (not filled). KiCad's mask-bridge allowance on U01 hides this from DRC.
where: Both boards, U01 openings. Rings reaching into an opening, with depth: DGND (136.35, 81.85) 0.035 mm; VDD_ADC (135.80, 80.23) 0.021 mm; DVDD (125.28, 79.54) 0.006 mm; STIM_CHB (131.71, 74.87) 0.003 mm; DVDD (130.521, 74.868) 0.0001 mm.
evidence: In this pass (check_b.py with the U01 F.Mask rectangles, mask_top.json and mask_bottom.json): vias with mask web under 0.09 mm, 93 (top) / 91 (bottom); under 0.05 mm, 63 / 61, all open. Five rings reach inside on each board. R2L-06 counted four on V3; the extra one is the VDD_ADC via at (135.80, 80.23), 0.021 mm into U01_BCD2's left inner-column opening. R2L-06 also found that 44-46 of the near vias carry a different net from the nearest finger, and that DRC with the U01 mask-bridge attribute removed reports 199 or more solder_mask_bridge errors.
source: JLCPCB PCB Capabilities (at least 0.09 mm between mask openings and neighbouring traces; mask dam 0.10 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay Advanced PCB Capabilities (minimum mask dam 3 mil), https://www.pcbway.com/advanced-pcb-capabilities.html. Both read 11 Nov 2026. Project: known/r2-layout.json R2L-06.
consequence: Via rings of other nets and open holes sit exposed 0.08-0.14 mm from bond fingers, plated with the finish. A wire or the bonding capillary can touch them, and plating chemistry can stay in the open holes.
suggested_action: Ask the bonding house whether exposed rings at the finger ends are acceptable. If not, trim the opening margin to 0 on the via side, move the five intruding vias, and fill and cap the vias next to the openings (AB-20).
verification: Re-measured on both V4 boards in this pass.

title: No flatness limit is set for the ASIC boards, although Hirose allows only 0.02 mm of bow across each DF40 and a standard order allows about 0.09-0.13 mm.
what: Hirose asks that the board bow no more than 0.02 mm at the middle of a DF40, measured against the connector's two ends. A normal fab order guarantees bow and twist only as a share of length: 0.75 % in PCBWay's normal class (and in IPC) and 0.5 % in its hardest class. Over the 17.5 mm connector that is about 0.13 mm and 0.09 mm. Each ASIC board carries a DF40 on both faces at the same spot, its top copper is about 53 % filled against 15-17 % on the bottom, and a 0.8 mm board would be eight times less stiff than 1.6 mm. No record or order text sets a flatness limit.
where: Both boards: J4 DF40C-80DP on F.Cu at (135.54, 71.005) and J3 DF40C-80DS on B.Cu at (135.54, 71.01). The connector bodies are 17.52 mm and 18.6 mm long.
evidence: Hirose catalog p21: board warpage at most 0.02 mm at the centre, relative to both ends of the connector. Hirose drawings: header length 17.52 mm (EDC3-311351-00), receptacle 18.6 mm (EDC3-311352-00), lead coplanarity 0.1 mm. 0.02 / 17.52 = 0.11 %. PCBWay Advanced item 35: bow and twist ≤ 0.75 % normal, < 0.5 % high. JLCPCB gives no value. Copper after refill (a review working file (not published)): top board F.Cu 53.3 %, inner layers 79-89 %, B.Cu 15.1 % (17.4 % on the bottom board). In this pass, board_stats.txt gives front copper 237.0 mm² against back 66.9 mm² (top board) and 79.0 mm² (bottom board). SYS-48 quotes the same Hirose line but acts only on the reflow count, and the LDOB-20 flatness note covers only Option B.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jan 2025, p21 ('Board Warpage'; 'Number of Reflow Cycles 2 max'), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Hirose drawings EDC3-311351-00 (DF40C-*DP-0.4V(51), sheet 1/3, rev 10), https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=2d&lang=en&num=DF40C-80DP-0.4V%2851%29, and EDC3-311352-00 (sheet 1/2, rev 5), https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=2d&lang=en&num=DF40C-80DS-0.4V%2851%29. Read from copies saved 11 Nov in review_2026-11-11/a review working file (not published) (sha256 837bfa3e…, c3a66fc1…, f8fe6b2f…), because hirose.com returned 403 on 12 Nov. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced items 27 and 35, https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html. JLCPCB PCB Capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. IPC-6012's 0.75 % for surface-mount boards: from memory, not re-read.
consequence: A board bowed more than paste and lead coplanarity can absorb leaves open or weak DF40 joints, which carry every rail and 44 chip lines per port, and no third reflow is allowed for rework. A bowed board also sits poorly on the wire bonder.
suggested_action: Ask the chosen fabricator what bow it can hold across the J3/J4 site, and write that limit on the order. Prefer 1.6 mm unless the fit demands 0.8 mm. Measure the first bare boards across J3/J4 before assembly.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. Copper areas re-read from board_stats.txt in this pass.

title: No build order or cleaning rule is recorded, although Hirose advises against cleaning the DF40s and the bond fingers sit 2.35 mm from J4's solder joints.
what: Both faces must be soldered before the dies are attached and bonded: J3 and 24 capacitors below, and J4, six capacitors and the hand-soldered J1 above. Wire bonds need clean gold, but J4's 80 solder joints are 2.35 mm from the nearest finger. Hirose advises against cleaning the DF40 and allows only two reflows. No file says which flux, cleaning method or step order to use.
where: Both V4 boards: J4 (F.Cu) is 2.353 mm from finger BITR<2> of U01_BCD2, C50 3.053 mm and C6 3.922 mm. J3 and 24 0201s are on B.Cu; J1 is through-hole.
evidence: pcbnew distances (a review working file (not published)). In this pass, from the V4 parts lists: J3 and 24 capacitors on the bottom, J4, J1 and six capacitors on top. Neither board nor schematic has any text, title block or assembly note.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jan 2025 edition, p21 Precautions (2 reflow cycles maximum; cleaning not recommended because it may impair mating), https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=catalogue&lang=en&series=DF40. Copy downloaded 11 Nov 2026: a review working file (not published), SHA-256 837bfa3e…. Bond-pad cleanliness: engineering judgement.
consequence: Either the dies are bonded onto fingers with flux residue, giving weak or non-sticking bonds on irreplaceable dies, or the boards are wet-cleaned against Hirose's advice, which can degrade DF40 mating.
suggested_action: Put the build order in the order notes: bottom-side reflow, then top-side (no third reflow), J1 by hand with no-clean flux, and no wet cleaning. Plasma-clean before die attach and bonding once Hirose and the bonding house confirm it suits fitted DF40s, or mask the finger area during SMT.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. Part sides re-read from the V4 parts.csv files in this pass.

title: The June board came back with a break-off tab stub on the probe edge, right under the die, and nothing in the V4 order keeps tabs off that edge.
what: The designer's whole-board photo of the June board shows a tab remnant on the bottom edge. It is a strip about 4.2 mm wide, standing 0.2-0.3 mm proud of the routed edge, with five half holes along it: mouse bites, the perforation that lets a panel tab snap off. It sits under the middle of the die. The June Gerbers do not draw it, so the fabricator chose that edge when it panelised the board. On V4 the same edge is where the probes leave both dies.
where: June board bottom edge (y 84.32), x about 128.2-132.4, under the die (x 126.3-134.4). V4: the bottom edge at y 84.4724 under U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2.
evidence: Slide 2 image4.png, pixels x 317-517, y 806-822 (zoom: a review working file (not published)). A grey band lies below the edge, with five semicircles about 0.77 mm apart; positions converted to board mm with the outline fit. PCB-Edge_Cuts.gbr is one closed outline with no tabs, and pcbway_fab has no panel drawing or order note.
source: S01 slide 2 image4.png (path in AB-12). W2/inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/PCB-Edge_Cuts.gbr. known/asic.json ASIC-28.

verification: Single reviewer (gap round), from the photo. The V4 bottom-edge position re-read in this pass.

title: The 8.1 x 7.0 mm die fits the 8.583 mm finger opening with only about 0.24 mm per side and 0.19 mm to the V4 row openings. The June board proves the fit with the designer's die and bonder, but V4 records neither die thickness nor bond recipe.

Centred, it leaves 0.242 mm per side to the inner side fingers. At that gap, Würth's chip-to-pad rule of 1.5 x chip thickness would need a die no thicker than about 0.16 mm. The June board had the same 8.583 mm opening and about the same 1.29 mm to the top row, and its photo shows every side wire bonded, so this geometry has been bonded once. V4's merged row openings start 0.191 mm from the die edges, 0.05 mm closer than June's per-finger openings. The V4 question list still asks for the die size, which the slides now give.
where: Both V4 boards: U01_BCD1/BCD2 inner side-finger columns (BCD1 opening x 125.8246-134.4077, BCD2 x 136.2103-144.7934), and the BCD1 row openings at x 125.519-125.875 and 134.358-134.712.
evidence: The opening is 8.5831 mm on both V4 and June, so a centred 8.1 mm die leaves 0.242 mm per side. Die top to the top row's inner edge: 1.32 mm with the die bottom at 84.0, or 1.79 mm at 84.47; June 1.29 mm. The V4 row openings sit 0.191 mm from the die edges (out/mask_check.json), June's 0.242 mm. Die thickness, wire type and the June bond recipe are in no file.
source: S01 slides 1-2 (path and hash in AB-12). June Gerbers W2/inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/PCB-F_Cu.gbr and PCB-F_Mask.gbr. ASIC_FE_2026-11-11/deliver10/report/index.html (question list). W2/inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 35 (8.1 x 7 mm). Würth Elektronik CBT, 'Chip on Board / Wire Bonding - Design Rules', V1.2 / 12.2021, chip-to-pad 1.5 x chip thickness, https://www.we-online.com/files/pdf1/design-rules-wire-bonding-cbt-en.pdf. A typical fillet and bleed width of 0.1-0.3 mm: from memory, not re-read.
consequence: Low risk if the V4 dies are thinned like the June die and bonded by the same house. A thicker die or a different bonder could find the 0.24 mm side gap and 0.19 mm mask margin too tight, or attach fillet could bleed onto the fingers.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer to confirm that the V4 dies come from the June lot (same thickness) and will use the same bonding recipe, and drop 'die size' from the question list. The die outline goes into the footprint with AB-12.
verification: Single reviewer (gap round). The 8.5831 mm opening and the row-opening x positions re-read from the V4 mask rectangles in this pass. Rated minor, where ASIC-11 was major, because the June bond demonstrates the fit.
also_known_as: ASIC-11; A-5 (die-size part, answered by slide 1)

title: The free end of every stack exposes all 80 live contacts, including +10 V and −10 V, and which connector is exposed depends on the port.
what: Both connectors are fitted on both boards. On the FPGA-LDO top-side port the far board's J4 plug is the free end. On the underside port the near board mates through its J4 plug, so the far ('top') board hangs lowest and its J3 receptacle is the free end. Either way the open connector carries every rail and signal, with VDD10 on pin 36 and VSS10 on pin 54 at 0.4 mm pitch. Assembly notes written from the top-side picture would be wrong for the underside port.
where: Both V4 boards: J3 DF40C-80DS on B.Cu and J4 DF40C-80DP on F.Cu, both fitted. FPGA-LDO A and router: J3 DF40C-80DP on top and J4 DF40C-80DS on the bottom, at (99.783, 113.51).
evidence: In this pass: J3/J4 are not DNP, are in the BOM, and J3.n = J4.n on 80/80 (V4 dumps). Connector types and sides from exports/ldo_a and exports/ldo_b_router parts.csv.
source: Engineering judgement. Project: known/pair-stacking.json F5; known/r2-system.json R2S-10.
consequence: Saline, a probe or a tool touching the open plug can short a rail or inject current into ASIC lines on a live head stage.
suggested_action: Use near/far wording in assembly and firmware notes. Choose a cover for the exposed plug or receptacle, or build one far-board variant per port with the unused connector not fitted.
verification: Connector types, sides and fit flags re-read in this pass.

title: Pin map V6 gives the top chips their own SPI_LATCH line without the 10 kΩ pull-down that holds the bottom chips' latch low before the FPGA is configured.
what: On FPGA-LDO A V12 the only pull resistor on an SPI line is R18, 10 kΩ from SPI_LATCH_SHARED to GND. It keeps the active-high latch off while the Frontend FPGA is unconfigured; with PUDC_B tied high, the FPGA's pins float until the bitstream loads. In V4 the top chips take their latch from pin 70 (T_SPI_LATCH). Pin map V6 turns the existing pin-70 lines (/ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out and /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out) into these latch outputs. Those lines have no resistor, and the Frontend pin file sets no pull-down. So after V6 the four top chips' latch would float through power-up and configuration.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: J3.70 /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out (to Frontend N3) and J4.70 /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out (to P4); R18 at (101.08, 124.9) on /SPI_LATCH_SHARED (J3.61, J4.61). Top board: /T_SPI_LATCH on J3/J4.70, U01_BCD1/BCD2.SPI_LATCH.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv and parts.csv: the pull resistors on ASIC nets are R2-R5 (STIM_*), R6 (AC_IN), R16 (FE_RESET), R17 (IMP_TST), R18 (SPI_LATCH_SHARED) and R19 (CHIP_RESET, pulled to ASIC_DVDD), all 10k. /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out and /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out have none (R18 re-read in this pass). known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv rows A,J3,70 and A,J4,70 (and the B rows) require ASIC7_8_TOP_SPI_LATCH and ASIC3_4_TOP_SPI_LATCH, marked 'rename (existing line)'. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 25 and 69 set only PACKAGE_PIN and IOSTANDARD. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md: PUDC_B is tied high. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4: SPI_LATCH is a positive pulse.
source: W2 files: exports/ldo_a; known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc; inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md. known/system.json SYS-28 (the floating window). Engineering judgement.
consequence: At power-up the top chips may latch whatever their floating SPI inputs hold. Stimulation stays off, because STIM_EN and STIM_START are pulled down, but half the ASICs start in an undefined configuration until the FPGA reloads it, and a floating input may draw extra current.
suggested_action: When the V6 routes are drawn, add 10 kΩ pull-downs like R18 on the two top-chip latch lines, and on Option B if it ever carries them. This is not needed if pin 70 is tied to /SPI_LATCH_SHARED instead (AB-28).
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. R18 and the FPGA-LDO A pin-70 nets re-read in this pass.

title: The V4 bond-finger fixes exist only in the boards' own copies of the die footprint, and U01's DNP flag does not stop KiCad plotting paste on the fingers.
what: V4 removed solder paste from all 352 bond fingers and added the row mask openings by editing the two U01 footprints inside each board. The footprint library 'chip' and the symbol library 'IC' are in neither project and not in the V4 zips, so no library holds the fixed footprint. Updating U01 from the designer's original library would bring back paste and the old per-finger mask. The DNP flag does not protect the fingers either: KiCad 10.0.6 still plots paste for a DNP part.
where: Both V4 boards: U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2 (chip:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP), F.Paste and F.Mask. Folders boards/asic_top and boards/asic_bottom, and deliver10/report/downloads/ASIC_*_Board_V4_KiCad.zip, which hold the PCB.* files only.
evidence: The received boards have F.Paste on all 352 die pads and V4 on none, with positions and sizes unchanged. V4 has 6 (BCD1) / 5 (BCD2) F.Mask rectangles, the received boards 0 (a review working file (not published)). DRC and ERC report that the configuration includes neither the footprint library 'chip' nor the symbol library 'IC' (exports/asic_*/drc.json and erc.json, re-read in this pass). A kicad-cli 10.0.6 F.Paste export of a received-board copy, with and without U01 set to DNP, gives 352 paste apertures both times (a review working file (not published)). In this pass: the V4 zips list only PCB.kicad_pcb, .kicad_sch, .kicad_pro and .kicad_prl, and V4 has 0 die pads with paste.
source: KiCad 9.0 PCB Editor manual, 'Updating and exchanging footprints', https://docs.kicad.org/9.0/en/pcbnew/pcbnew.html#updating-and-exchanging-footprints. The owner's rule that libraries are project-local, AGENTS.md. Project: known/asic_open.json P-M6; known/asic.json ASIC-19.
consequence: One footprint update during a later edit puts paste back on the bond fingers. The stencil then prints solder where wires must bond, and the boards are scrap.
suggested_action: Save the V4 U01 footprint and symbol into a project-local library used by both projects, and include it in the zips. Note that U01 must not be updated from the original 'chip' library.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. Zip contents, the DRC library warnings and the 0 paste pads re-checked in this pass.

Gerbers from either board get the same file names and the same X2 project ID with revision 'rev?', and the June PCBWay set has that ID too. Only the folder or zip name says which board and which version a file set is.

evidence: In this pass: line 5 of both .kicad_sch files is uuid f1e48754-5062-4826-a371-e5e4549ddf6b; both .kicad_pro files have SHA-256 3c7e0a11…; neither file type has a title_block; text_variables is {}. kicad-cli 10.0.6 Gerbers (a review working file (not published) and gerb_bottom): 33 identically named files per board. Both PCB-F_Cu.gtl files start with %TF.ProjectId,PCB,5043422e-6b69-4636-9164-5f7063625858,rev?*%, and both job files say Name 'PCB', Revision 'rev?'. inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/PCB-F_Cu.gbr line 3 carries the same ProjectId.

title: J3, J4 and the second chip lie outside the A2 sheet on both V4 schematics, so the schematic PDFs show neither connector nor U01_BCD2.
what: Both V4 schematics use an A2 page (594 x 420 mm), but J3, J4 and U01_BCD2 sit at y 514-516 mm, below the sheet border. A PDF holds only the page, so the exported and delivered PDFs show U01_BCD1 and the capacitors but none of the 80-pin connector map and not the second chip. The T_DISC_OUT(2) label is also off the page. The original PCB-5 schematic had everything inside the frame. The sheet also carries no notes or references, which the owner's schematic rules ask for.
where: boards/asic_top|asic_bottom/PCB.kicad_sch: J3 at (306.07, 514.35), J4 at (365.76, 515.62), U01_BCD2 at (144.78, 515.62). PDFs: exports/asic_*/schematic.pdf and deliver10/report/downloads/ASIC_Top_Board_V4_Schematic.pdf and ASIC_Bottom_Board_V4_Schematic.pdf.
evidence: In this pass: paper 'A2' and the three symbol positions in both files. Outside the frame on both boards: 3 of 35 symbols, 214 of 361 labels and 270 of 723 wires, with wires reaching y 622.3 mm (a review working file (not published)). All four PDFs are one page, MediaBox 1683.79 x 1190.52 pt. The wires span x 38.1-457.2 mm and y 15.2-622.3 mm, so A1 landscape would still clip them, while A1 portrait holds everything. PCB-5 (review_2026-11-11/boards/asic/PCB.kicad_sch) had J3 at (77.47, 79.375), J4 at (137.16, 80.645) and U01_BCD2 at (394.97, 264.795), with nothing outside the frame.

title: Shared control lines drive up to 16 die pads from one FPGA pin, and the ASIC's input load is not recorded.
what: STIM_CHB, FE_RESET and CHIP_RESET each reach 4 die pads per board, so 16 per FPGA pin across both ports. STIM_EN, STIM_CLK, STIM_START, IMP_TEST and AC_IN each reach 8, and CLKH reaches 4 per port. Each board adds a 17-47 mm branch. Without the die's input capacitance and leakage, the edge rate and the pull-resistor sizing cannot be checked.
where: FPGA-LDO A nets STIM_*_SHARED, FE_RESET_SHARED, CHIP_RESET_SHARED, IMP_TST_SHARED, ASIC_AC_IN and BOARD1/3_CLK; the die pads on both V4 boards.
evidence: In this pass, die pads per V4 board: CHIP_RESET 4, FE_RESET 4, STIM_CHB 4, STIM_EN/CLK/START 2 each, IMP_TEST 2, AC_IN 2, CLKH 2. pair-stacking F6 (received boards, same routing): branch lengths per stack CHIP_RESET 47.33 + 43.28 mm and CLKH 40.20 + 39.60 mm. FPGA-LDO A has 10k pulls R2-R6 and R16-R19, and AC_IN has no driver.
source: Engineering judgement. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03 (input limits absent). known/pair-stacking.json F6.
consequence: Probably fine at these lengths, but a slow or ringing CHIP_RESET or STIM_CLK edge would hit all eight chips at once.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for input capacitance and leakage per pad, then re-run the stack signal model with 16 loads.
verification: Die-pad counts re-read on both V4 boards in this pass. Branch lengths from the morning pair review.

title: Eleven via barrels per board carry +10 V or −10 V through the opposite stimulator plane, with only 0.127 mm of laminate between hole wall and plane copper.
what: Where a VDD10 via passes the VSS10 plane, or a VSS10 via passes the VDD10 plane, the hole wall is 0.127 mm from copper with about 20 V across it. Another 104 via-to-plane sites per board have 10-11.5 V across the same gap. Under humidity and bias, copper filaments can grow along the glass fibres from a hole wall to a nearby plane; this is called conductive anodic filament (CAF). A head-mounted board runs warm and humid, and four of the 20 V vias sit 0.17-0.21 mm from the routed edge.
evidence: hv_holes.py on refilled scratch copies (a review working file (not published)): 115 via-layer sites per board with the hole wall under 0.20 mm from plane copper at 10 V or more difference. All are at 0.127 mm (0.125 mm ring radius + 0.0762 mm clearance − 0.075 mm hole radius), and 11 are at 20 V. Hole wall to routed edge for the four edge vias: 0.166-0.205 mm. In this pass, the 11 via positions and spans were confirmed on both V4 boards.
source: Engineering judgement on CAF; no fabricator or laminate CAF limit was found. JLCPCB PCB Capabilities (inner-layer via hole to copper 0.2 mm), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. PCBWay PCB Capabilities, Advanced item 13 (hole to copper on 10+ layers: ≥ 10 mil normal, 7-8 mil high), https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html.
consequence: Unlikely within one study, but a filament between +10 V and −10 V would short the stimulator rails inside the board, where it cannot be seen or repaired.
suggested_action: Where there is room, open the VSS10 clearances around VDD10 vias, and the VDD10 clearances around VSS10 vias, to at least 0.25 mm from the hole wall. Keep these vias off the routed edge, and ask the fabricator for a CAF-resistant laminate.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. VDD10/VSS10 via positions and spans re-read in this pass.

consequence: A fabricator may query it. If a panel rail is close, a copper line could be plated beside the probe edge.
suggested_action: Move the dimension to a User or Fab layer before plotting order files.
verification: Single reviewer (gap round). The dimension's layer and extent re-read in this pass.

title: Every inner plane is one piece, but some plane regions hang on narrow necks, and on V4 KiCad itself flags a 0.0625 mm neck in the REF_VCM plane on the top board's In4.
what: An opening test on V3 found plane regions joined to the rest only through necks narrower than 0.25 mm; the narrowest, 0.12-0.15 mm, was on VSS10 (In6) of the top board. On V4 every inner plane is still one piece. DRC now reports one REF_VCM connection only 0.0625 mm wide on the top board's In4, between the clearances of the DGND vias at (134.08, 82.46) and (134.13, 83.07). This is the 'new connection-width warning' the V4 report mentions. Rail currents are milliamps, so it matters only for etching.
where: Top board V4, In4.Cu, near (134.1, 82.84). The V3 necks are listed in R2L-08.
evidence: In this pass: exports/asic_top/drc.json has a connection_width warning, 'actual 0.0625 mm', on zone 'REF_VCM plane', In4. Fill vertices at (134.11, 82.81-82.84) and (134.05-134.17, 82.87-82.88) lie between the two via clearances (a review working file (not published)). The In1-In8 fills are one piece each on both boards (planes2.py).
source: Board files and KiCad DRC; known/r2-layout.json R2L-08; engineering judgement.
consequence: No DC effect. A sliver this narrow may etch away or be flagged by the fabricator's CAM system.
suggested_action: When the deep vias are converted (AB-02), nudge one of the two DGND vias or add a small no-fill area, so the sliver is removed or widened above 0.0762 mm.
verification: DRC warning and fill geometry re-read on V4 in this pass. The V3 neck test was not re-run on V4.

title: KiCad ERC cannot check the V4 pin map, because every die pin and every connector pin is typed passive.
what: The U01 symbol gives all 176 die pins the passive type, and so do the generic J3/J4 symbols. KiCad lets passive pins connect to almost anything, so ERC would not flag two chip outputs on one net or an undriven chip input. On V4 the 12 ERC errors are the BIT pads and the rest are drawing leftovers. The pin map is correct today, but only a script shows it.
where: Both V4 schematics: symbol IC:U01_BCD_OFF_CHIP (176 pins) and J3/J4 Conn_02x40_Odd_Even; exports/asic_top|asic_bottom/erc.json.
evidence: Each symbol has 176 passive pins, 0 hidden, 176 unique numbers. ERC per board, re-read in this pass: 12 pin_not_connected, 193 unconnected wire ends, 277 off-grid points, 1 stray no-connect flag at (255.27, 53.34), and 2+2 library warnings. The top board also has 2 isolated_pin_label warnings (T_DISC_OUT, T_DISC_OUT(2)). A stack check combining both netlists (a review working file (not published)) finds every one of the 80 pins with 0 or 1 output: 44 chip outputs plus 2 DISC_OUT per port, and no spare pin.
source: KiCad 9.0 Schematic Editor manual, pin electrical types and the ERC table, https://docs.kicad.org/9.0/en/eeschema/eeschema.html.
consequence: A later change to the pin order, or a rework, can re-create output contention or a floating chip input while ERC still looks clean.
suggested_action: Give the U01 symbol pin types from the designer's sheet (outputs, inputs, power), add no-connect flags on the BIT pads once the designer confirms them, and keep the stack-check script with the project.
verification: Checked by an independent reviewer. ERC counts re-read in this pass.
